<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

1	# richgo
2	
3	Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.
4	
5	[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)
6	
7	## Description
8	
9	richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.
10	
11	## Installation
12	
13	### Using go get
14	
15	```
16	go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
17	```
18	
19	### Using homebrew
20	
21	```
22	brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
23	```
24	
25	### Using asdf
26	
27	```
28	asdf plugin add richgo
29	asdf install richgo 0.3.6
30	```
31	
32	## Usage
33	
34	### Basic Usage
35	
36	```sh
37	richgo test ./...
38	```
39	
40	### In an existing pipeline
41	
42	If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.
43	
44	For example:
45	
46	```sh
47	go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
48	```
49	
50	This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.
51	
52	### Creating an alias
53	
54	You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:
55	
56	* bash: `~/.bashrc`
57	* zsh: `~/.zshrc`
58	
59	```
60	alias go=richgo
61	```
62	
63	## Configuration
64	
65	### Configuration file paths
66	
67	It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:
68	
69	* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
70	* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
71	* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
72	* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
73	* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
74	* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
75	* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
76	* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
77	* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
78	* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
79	* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
80	* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`
81	
82	Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.
83	
84	### Configuration file format
85	
86	Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.
87	
88	```yaml
89	# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
90	labelType: (long | short | none)
91	
92	# Style of "Build" lines.
93	buildStyle:
94	  # Hide lines
95	  hide: (true | false)
96	  # Bold or increased intensity.
97	  bold: (true | false)
98	  faint: (true | false)
99	  italic: (true | false)
100	  underline: (true | false)
101	  blinkSlow: (true | false)
102	  blinkRapid: (true | false)
103	  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
104	  inverse: (true | false)
105	  conceal: (true | false)
106	  crossOut: (true | false)
107	  frame: (true | false)
108	  encircle: (true | false)
109	  overline: (true | false)
110	  # Fore-color of text
111	  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
112	  # Back-color of text
113	  background: # Same format as `foreground`
114	
115	# Style of the "Start" lines.
116	startStyle:
117	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
118	
119	# Style of the "Pass" lines.
120	passStyle:
121	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
122	
123	# Style of the "Fail" lines.
124	failStyle:
125	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
126	
127	# Style of the "Skip" lines.
128	skipStyle:
129	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
130	
131	# Style of the "File" lines.
132	fileStyle:
133	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
134	
135	# Style of the "Line" lines.
136	lineStyle:
137	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
138	
139	# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
140	passPackageStyle:
141	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
142	
143	# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
144	failPackageStyle:
145	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
146	
147	# A threshold of the coverage
148	coverThreshold: (0-100)
149	
150	# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
151	coveredStyle:
152	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
153	
154	# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
155	uncoveredStyle:
156	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
157	
158	# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
159	removals:
160	  - (regexp)
161	# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
162	leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
163	```
164	
165	### Line categories
166	
167	Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:
168	
169	* **Build**: Build error messages
170	* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
171	* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
172	* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
173	* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
174	* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
175	* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
176	* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines
177	
178	Each category can be styled separately.
179	
180	### Label types
181	
182	* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
183	* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
184	* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.
185	
186	### Default configuration
187	
188	```yaml
189	labelType: long
190	buildStyle:
191	  bold: true
192	  foreground: yellow
193	startStyle:
194	  foreground: lightBlack
195	passStyle:
196	  foreground: green
197	failStyle:
198	  bold: true
199	  foreground: red
200	skipStyle:
201	  foreground: lightBlack
202	passPackageStyle:
203	  foreground: green
204	  hide: true
205	failPackageStyle:
206	  bold: true
207	  foreground: red
208	  hide: true
209	coverThreshold: 50
210	coveredStyle:
211	  foreground: green
212	uncoveredStyle:
213	  bold: true
214	  foreground: yellow
215	fileStyle:
216	  foreground: cyan
217	lineStyle:
218	  foreground: magenta
219	```
220	
221	### Solarized Dark theme compatibility
222	
223	The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.
224	
225	To resolve that conflict, you can set another color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle" in your `.richstyle` file:
226	
227	```yaml
228	startStyle:
229	  foreground: yellow
230	
231	skipStyle:
232	  foreground: lightYellow
233	```
234	
235	## Overriding colorization detection
236	
237	By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.
238	
239	To force colorization, add `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` to the environment:
240	
241	```sh
242	RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 richgo test ./... | tee test.log
243	```
244	
245	## Getting the version
246	
247	If you want to get the version of `richgo`, this information is embedded in the binary (since Go 1.18). You can view it with `go version -m`:
248	
249	```console
250	$ go version -m $(command -v richgo)
251	./richgo: go1.18
252		path	github.com/kyoh86/richgo
253		mod	github.com/kyoh86/richgo	v0.3.10	h1:iSGvcjhtQN2IVrBDhPk0if0R/RMQnCN1E/9OyAW4UUs=
254		[...]
255	```
256	
257	With POSIX `awk`:
258	
259	```console
260	$ go version -m $(command -v richgo) | awk '$1 == "mod" && $2 == "github.com/kyoh86/richgo" {print $3;}'
261	v0.3.10
262	```
263	
264	## License
265	
266	This is distributed under the [MIT License](http://www.opensource.org/licenses/MIT).

YOUR ASSIGNED DOMAIN:
{{item}}

items: DOMAIN 1 — Default-config line classification & label rendering. With no config file (run in an empty temp dir as CWD) and RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1, feed `testfilter` every kind of `go test` output line and record exact transformed bytes: `=== RUN   TestX`, `=== RUN   TestX/Sub`, indented variants (e.g. `    --- PASS: TestX/Sub (0.00s)`), `=== PAUSE`, `=== CONT`, `--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)`, `--- FAIL: TestX (0.01s)`, `--- SKIP: TestX (0.00s)`, `--- BENCH`, bare `PASS`, bare `FAIL`, bare `SKIP`?, `ok  \texample.com/p\t0.002s`, `ok  example.com/p 0.002s` (spaces), `FAIL\texample.com/p\t0.002s`, `?   \texample.com/p\t[no test files]`, `# example.com/p` build error headers, compiler error lines like `./main.go:3:2: undefined: x`, test log lines like `    foo_test.go:12: message`, `=== NAME`, `=== RUN TestX` (single space variants), benchmark result lines (`BenchmarkX-8\t...`), panic output, `FAIL\texample.com/p [build failed]`, lines with `[no tests to run]`, `testing: warning: no tests to run`. Determine: which categories exist, the exact label text+padding per category (long labels), where the `|` separator goes, how `Test` prefix stripping works (default leaveTestPrefix=false), how leading indentation is handled, which lines are hidden by default (bare PASS/FAIL?), and how unrecognized/plain lines are rendered. Also test `labelType` variations only if trivial via stdin — otherwise leave to other domains.

DOMAIN 2 — Coverage rendering. With default config and RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1, feed `testfilter` coverage lines: `coverage: 0.0% of statements`, `coverage: 49.9% of statements`, `coverage: 50.0% of statements`, `coverage: 75.5% of statements`, `coverage: 100.0% of statements`, `coverage: 33.3% of statements in ./...`, `ok  \texample.com/p\t0.002s\tcoverage: 80.0% of statements`, and other plausible variants. Record exact bytes: the `[#######___]` progress bar rendering rule (width, rounding: how many # for 0/5/49.9/50/75.5/95/100%), the covered vs uncovered style threshold behavior (exactly at 50?), and whether the `ok`+coverage combined line renders differently. Then, in temp dirs, write `.richstyle` files with different `coverThreshold` values (0, 30, 100) and re-test to map threshold semantics (< vs <=). Also test malformed coverage lines (missing %, non-numeric).

DOMAIN 3 — Config file discovery & parsing. In temp dirs, test which config files `testfilter` loads: `$CWD/.richstyle`, `.richstyle.yaml`, `.richstyle.yml` (precedence when several exist), `$HOME/.richstyle*`, `$GOPATH/.richstyle*` (set GOPATH to temp), `$GOROOT/.richstyle*` (careful: setting GOROOT may break delegation to `go`; test only with testfilter, and check whether GOROOT config is actually read), and `RICHGO_LOCAL=1` semantics. Test: partial configs (only one key set — do defaults merge or reset?), empty config file, invalid YAML (what error, exit code, stdout vs stderr), unknown keys (ignored or error?), wrong types (e.g. `labelType: 5`, `coverThreshold: abc`, `coverThreshold: 150`, negative). Report exact error messages and exit codes, and whether output is still produced after config errors.

DOMAIN 4 — Style attributes & color syntax. In temp dirs with `.richstyle` files, enumerate the exact ANSI escape sequences for every style boolean attribute on one category (e.g. passStyle): bold, faint, italic, underline, blinkSlow, blinkRapid, inverse, conceal, crossOut, frame, encircle, overline, hide — the order they are emitted, reset behavior (ESC[0m placement — note the observed quirk where a BUILD line's reset appears at the start of the NEXT line). Then enumerate foreground/background color syntaxes: all named colors that work (try black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, lightBlack/lightRed/.../lightWhite, gray, grey, lightGray, darkGray, etc.) with their exact codes; `#rgb`? / `#rrggbb` hex (exact truecolor codes); `rgb(1,2,3)` decimal and `rgb(0x01,0x02,0x03)` hex forms; invalid color names/codes (error message? fallback?). Also: background+foreground together, attribute+color combination ordering, and `hide: true` semantics per category.

DOMAIN 5 — `removals` and `leaveTestPrefix`. In temp dirs with `.richstyle`: test `removals` with one/multiple regexps (which lines get dropped — matched anywhere in line? anchored? applied before or after classification? does a removed line vanish entirely or print blank?), invalid regex behavior (error message, exit code), regex escaping in YAML. Test `leaveTestPrefix: true` vs default false on `=== RUN   TestFoo`, `--- PASS: TestFoo (0.00s)`, subtests `TestFoo/SubBar`, names without `Test` prefix (`Testfoo`, `Testify`, `TEST`, `BenchmarkX`), and on both forced-color and plain output. Also check interaction: does leaveTestPrefix affect package lines or only test lines?

DOMAIN 6 — `test` subcommand, delegation, exit codes, TTY detection. Create a temp Go module with a passing package and a failing package (GOFLAGS=-mod=mod, set GO111MODULE if needed; use only stdlib; no network — set GOPROXY=off). Run `/workspace/executable test ./...`, `/workspace/executable test -v ./...`, `/workspace/executable test -count=1 .` etc. and compare with `go test` output: does richgo add/remove flags (e.g. force `-v`?), how does it pipe output, what exit code on test failure vs success vs build error, does stderr pass through? Test delegation: `/workspace/executable version`, `/workspace/executable env GOPATH`, `/workspace/executable build` in the module, unknown command `/workspace/executable frobnicate` (exit code, stderr), no args (exit code). How is `go` located (PATH? does it work if PATH lacks go — try env with restricted PATH)? TTY detection: use `script -qec '/workspace/executable testfilter' /dev/null` with piped stdin, or `script` to give it a PTY stdout, and confirm colorization on TTY without RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR. Test RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR values: 0, empty, false, garbage — which enable color? Test `testfilter` with extra args (`/workspace/executable testfilter foo`) and `richgo test --help` behavior.

DOMAIN 7 — Input edge cases & non-color passthrough. Without RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR (piped stdout), map exact passthrough semantics: input ending with/without trailing newline, empty input, single newline, CRLF line endings (are  preserved? do they affect classification when color forced?), lines with only spaces, invalid UTF-8 bytes, very long lines (test 64KB, 1MB single line — scanner buffer limit? error message? exit code?), and input that looks like test output but piped (no color): is it passed through 100% verbatim plus what trailing bytes exactly (od -c the outputs)? Also with forced color: same edge cases (CRLF, invalid UTF-8, long lines). Confirm the trailing-newline rule in both modes precisely: for inputs `''`, `'
'`, `'a'`, `'a
'`, `'a
b'`, `'a
b
'` record exact output bytes with od -c, both plain and forced-color modes.

# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo

### Using asdf

```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
  blinkSlow: (true | false)
  blinkRapid: (true | false)
  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
  inverse: (true | false)
  conceal: (true | false)
  crossOut: (true | false)
  frame: (true | false)
  encircle: (true | false)
  overline: (true | false)
  # Fore-color of text
  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
  # Back-color of text
  background: # Same format as `foreground`

# Style of the "Start" lines.
startStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" lines.
passStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" lines.
failStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Skip" lines.
skipStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "File" lines.
fileStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Line" lines.
lineStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
passPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
failPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# A threshold of the coverage
coverThreshold: (0-100)

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
coveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
uncoveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
removals:
  - (regexp)
# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
```

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

### Default configuration

```yaml
labelType: long
buildStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
startStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passStyle:
  foreground: green
failStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
skipStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passPackageStyle:
  foreground: green
  hide: true
failPackageStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
  hide: true
coverThreshold: 50
coveredStyle:
  foreground: green
uncoveredStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
fileStyle:
  foreground: cyan
lineStyle:
  foreground: magenta
```

### Solarized Dark theme compatibility

The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.

To resolve that conflict, you can set another color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle" in your `.richstyle` file:

```yaml
startStyle:
  foreground: yellow

skipStyle:
  foreground: lightYellow
```

## Overriding colorization detection

By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.

To force colorization, add `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` to the environment:

```sh
RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 richgo test ./... | tee test.log
```

## Getting the version

If you want to get the version of `richgo`, this information is embedded in the binary (since Go 1.18). You can view it with `go version -m`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo)
./richgo: go1.18
	path	github.com/kyoh86/richgo
	mod	github.com/kyoh86/richgo	v0.3.10	h1:iSGvcjhtQN2IVrBDhPk0if0R/RMQnCN1E/9OyAW4UUs=
	[...]
```

With POSIX `awk`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo) | awk '$1 == "mod" && $2 == "github.com/kyoh86/richgo" {print $3;}'
v0.3.10
```

Go is a tool for managing Go source code.

Usage:

	go <command> [arguments]

The commands are:

	bug         start a bug report
	build       compile packages and dependencies
	clean       remove object files and cached files
	doc         show documentation for package or symbol
	env         print Go environment information
	fix         update packages to use new APIs
	fmt         gofmt (reformat) package sources
	generate    generate Go files by processing source
	get         add dependencies to current module and install them
	install     compile and install packages and dependencies
	list        list packages or modules
	mod         module maintenance
	work        workspace maintenance
	run         compile and run Go program
	test        test packages
	tool        run specified go tool
	version     print Go version
	vet         report likely mistakes in packages

Use "go help <command>" for more information about a command.

76	* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`

79	* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`

105	  conceal: (true | false)
106	  crossOut: (true | false)

108	  encircle: (true | false)
109	  overline: (true | false)

114

117	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
118	
119	# Style of the "Pass" lines.
120	passStyle:
121	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
122	
123	# Style of the "Fail" lines.
124	failStyle:
125	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
126	
127	# Style of the "Skip" lines.
128	skipStyle:
129	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
130	
131	# Style of the "File" lines.
132	fileStyle:
133	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
134	
135	# Style of the "Line" lines.
136	lineStyle:
137	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
138	
139	# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
140	passPackageStyle:
141	  # Same format as `buildStyle`
142

146

149

151	coveredStyle:

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
EXIT: 0

args.command: T=$(mktemp -d) && echo "$T" && cd "$T" && printf '=== RUN   TestX\n' | RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 /workspace/executable testfilter | od -c | head -20; echo "exit=$?"

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

### Default configuration

```yaml
labelType: long
buildStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
startStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passStyle:
  foreground: green
failStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
skipStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passPackageStyle:
  foreground: green
  hide: true
failPackageStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
  hide: true
coverThreshold: 50
coveredStyle:
  foreground: green
uncoveredStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
fileStyle:
  foreground: cyan
lineStyle:
  foreground: magenta
```

### Solarized Dark theme compatibility

The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.

To resolve that conflict, you can set another color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle" in your `.richstyle` file:

```yaml
startStyle:
  foreground: yellow

skipStyle:
  foreground: lightYellow
```

## Overriding colorization detection

By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.

To force colorization, add `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` to the environment:

```sh
RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 richgo test ./... | tee test.log
```

payload.resultSummary:
All experiments done; temp dirs cleaned up. Here is the complete behavioral spec for Domain 2 (Coverage rendering).

# DOMAIN 2 — Coverage rendering spec (`testfilter`, `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`, default config)

## 1. Which lines are treated as Cover lines

A line is a Cover line **only if it exactly matches** (anchored at both start and end of the line):

```
coverage: <digits>.<one digit>% of statements
```

- Exactly one decimal digit required: `50.0%` matches; `50%`, `50.00%`, `33.33%` do NOT.
- Trailing/leading anything breaks the match: `... of statements in ./...`, `... of statements in foo`, leading spaces or a leading tab, missing `%`, missing `of statements`, non-numeric value — all NOT Cover lines.
- No range validation: `105.0%` and even negative like `-5.0%`... — correction: `-5.0%` did NOT match (regex likely `\d+\.\d`); `105.0%` DID match (bar clamped).
- Non-matching lines fall into the "other/none" category: emitted uncolored with a blank 5-char label: `     | <original line>` + `\n`. Example: input `coverage: 33.3% of statements in ./...` → output `     | coverage: 33.3% of statements in ./...\n` (original line preserved verbatim after the label).

## 2. Cover line rendering (default config)

Input `coverage: 49.9% of statements\n` → exact output bytes:

```
ESC[33m ESC[1m COVER| 49.9% [####______] ESC[0m \n
```

i.e. `1b 5b 33 33 6d 1b 5b 31 6d 43 4f 56 45 52 7c 20 34 39 2e 39 25 20 5b 23 23 23 23 5f 5f 5f 5f 5f 5f 5d 1b 5b 30 6d 0a`

Input `coverage: 50.0% of statements\n` →

```
ESC[32m COVER| 50.0% [#####_____] ESC[0m \n
```

Structure: `<style-open>COVER| <pct>% [<bar>]ESC[0m\n`

- Label `COVER|` followed by one space, then the percent text as parsed/reformatted (`49.9%`), one space, then the bar in square brackets.
- Uncovered style (below threshold): `ESC[33mESC[1m` (yellow foreground, then bold — note order: foreground escape first, then bold).
- Covered style: `ESC[32m` (green foreground, no bold).
- Style wraps the whole line including label and bar; single `ESC[0m` at end, then `\n` (added even if input lacks trailing newline).

## 3. Progress bar rule

- Width: **10 characters** inside `[...]`; `#` for filled, `_` for empty.
- Filled count = **truncation toward zero of pct/10** (equivalently `int(pct)/10` integer division), clamped to max 10. Observed:

| pct | # count | | pct | # count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 0 | | 54.9 / 55.0 / 55.1 | 5 |
| 5.0 / 9.9 | 0 | | 75.5 | 7 |
| 10.0 / 14.9 / 15.0 / 15.1 | 1 | | 85.0 | 8 |
| 20.0 / 25.0 | 2 | | 90.0 | 9 |
| 33.3 | 3 | | 95.0 / 99.9 | 9 |
| 49.9 | 4 | | 100.0 / 105.0 | 10 (clamped) |
| 50.0 / 50.1 | 5 | | | |

Key boundary evidence: `15.0`→1, `55.0`→5 (so it's floor/truncation, not rounding).

## 4. Threshold semantics (coveredStyle vs uncoveredStyle)

- **Covered when pct >= coverThreshold** (inclusive). Verified: default 50 → 49.9 uncovered, 50.0 covered. `coverThreshold: 30` → 29.9 uncovered, 30.0/30.1 covered. `coverThreshold: 0` → 0.0 covered (green). `coverThreshold: 100` → 99.9 uncovered, 100.0 covered.
- **Config styles merge field-by-field with the defaults.** With `.richstyle` containing `coverThreshold: 60`, `coveredStyle: {foreground: cyan}`, `uncoveredStyle: {foreground: magenta, underline: true}`:
  - `60.0`/`80.0` → `ESC[36mCOVER| ...` (cyan, no bold)
  - `59.9` → `ESC[35m ESC[1m ESC[4mCOVER| 59.9% [#####_____]ESC[0m` — magenta + **bold (inherited from default uncoveredStyle)** + underline. Escape order observed: foreground, bold, underline.

## 5. `ok` + coverage combined line

Input `ok  \texample.com/p\t0.002s\tcoverage: 80.0% of statements\n` →

```
ESC[32mPASS | example.com/p coverage: 80.0% of statementsESC[0m\n
```

- Classified as PassPackage (green), NOT as a Cover line: **no progress bar, no threshold styling** — `coverage: 20.0%` on an `ok` line renders identically green.
- The `ok  \t` prefix is replaced by label `PASS | `; the elapsed-time field `\t0.002s\t` is removed and collapses to a single space before `coverage:`; the coverage text is kept verbatim.

## 6. Pass-through mode (no FORCE_COLOR, stdout not TTY)

- Lines are passed through **unmodified** (no label, no bar, tabs preserved): input `coverage: 80.0% of statements\n` → identical output; input `ok  \texample.com/p\t0.002s\tcoverage: 80.0% of statements\n` → identical output.
- **Anomaly (applies to all lines, not just coverage): every output line is followed by an extra blank line** — observed `hello world\n` → `hello world\n\n`, and coverage lines likewise (`line\n\n`). In FORCE_COLOR mode there is no extra blank line. (Possibly an upstream-domain behavior, but flagged since an implementer must reproduce it.)
- Exit code 0 in all cases tested (including malformed lines and missing trailing newline).

payload.resultSummary:
# DOMAIN 7 — Input edge cases & non-color passthrough: behavioral spec

All experiments run from a fresh `mktemp -d` (no config files), piping stdin to `/workspace/executable testfilter`. Temp dir cleaned up afterward. "Plain mode" = piped stdout, no `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR`. "Color mode" = `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`.

## 1. Plain (non-color) mode — line processing + verbatim passthrough

**Core rule:** input is processed line-by-line with exactly `bufio.ScanLines` semantics (split on `
`; strip at most ONE trailing `` per line, including a lone `` at EOF). Each resulting line is written to stdout as `line + "
"`, **completely verbatim otherwise — zero classification, zero styling, zero hiding** (bare `PASS`/`FAIL`/`ok pkg` lines pass through untouched). Then:

- **stdout gets one extra `
` iff the input was empty OR ended with `
`.**
- **stderr always gets exactly one `
`** at the end (regardless of input).
- Exit code always `0` (even for binary garbage, NUL bytes, 100MB lines).

Exact byte matrix (stdout shown; stderr is always `
`):

| input | stdout bytes | why |
|---|---|---|
| `''` | `0a` | no lines + extra `
` (empty input) |
| `'
'` | `0a 0a` | one empty line + extra `
` |
| `'a'` | `61 0a` | one line, no trailing-NL so no extra |
| `'a
'` | `61 0a 0a` | one line + extra |
| `'a
b'` | `61 0a 62 0a` | no extra |
| `'a
b
'` | `61 0a 62 0a 0a` | extra |
| `'a

'` | `61 0a 0a 0a` | empty line preserved + extra |
| `'

'` | `0a 0a 0a` | |
| `''` | `0a` | lone `` at EOF stripped → one empty line, no trailing-NL → no extra |
| `'
'` | `0a 0a` | CR stripped, ends with `
` → extra |
| `'a
b
'` | `61 0a 62 0a 0a` | CRs stripped |
| `'a
'` | `61 0d 0a 0a` | **only one** trailing CR stripped per line |
| `'ab
'` | `61 0d 62 0a 0a` | interior `` preserved verbatim |
| `'   
	
'` | `20 20 20 0a 09 0a 0a` | whitespace-only lines preserved |
| `'a\xff\xfe
\x80
'` | `61 ff fe 0a 80 0a 0a` | invalid UTF-8 verbatim, exit 0 |
| `'a\x00b
'` | `61 00 62 0a 0a` | NUL verbatim |

With `2>&1`, `'a
'` yields `61 0a 0a 0a` — both trailing newlines come after all content (order between the stdout extra and the stderr one not distinguishable this way).

**No size limit:** single lines of 65535/65536/65537/70000/1MiB/10MiB/100MiB bytes all pass through fine (output = input+1 byte), exit 0, stderr `
`. NOT a default 64KB `bufio.Scanner` (or the buffer was raised); no error message anywhere. Same in color mode (1MiB and 10MiB tested: output = `     | ` prefix + line + `
`, exit 0).

## 2. Color mode (`RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`) — edge cases

Same ScanLines splitting and one-CR stripping, but semantics differ from plain mode:

- **No extra trailing newline, nothing on stderr, ever.** Output is exactly one decorated line per kept input line.
- **Empty lines (zero-length after CR-strip) are dropped entirely**: `''`→empty, `'
'`→empty, `'


'`→empty, `'a

b
'`→ only the `a` and `b` lines.
- **Whitespace-only lines are NOT empty** and get the uncategorized treatment: `'   '`→`20 20 20 20 20 7c 20 20 20 20 0a` (`"     |    
"`), `'	'`→`"     | 	
"`.
- **Uncategorized lines** are emitted as `20 20 20 20 20 7c 20` + line + `0a` — i.e. 5 spaces, `|`, space (long-label column, blank label), NO color escapes, content verbatim (including invalid UTF-8, NUL, interior ``).
- `'a'` vs `'a
'` → identical output (`     | a
`); trailing newline of input is irrelevant in color mode.
- CRLF: `` stripped before classification — `'a
b
'`→`     | a
     | b
`; `PASS
FAIL
`→ **empty output** (bare PASS/FAIL still hidden per default config). With `'--- FAIL: TestBar (0.00s)
'` one `` survives and is emitted *inside* the styled segment: `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | Bar (0.00s)ESC[0m
`.
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes never cause errors (exit 0) and are passed through verbatim, but they **can affect classification**:
  - `'--- FAIL: T\xffest (0.00s)
'` → NOT classified (falls to `     | --- FAIL: T\xffest (0.00s)`).
  - `'--- FAIL: TestBar (0.00s)\xff
'` → classified FAIL; the `\xff` is emitted inside the style: `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | Bar (0.00s)\xffESC[0m
`.
  - `'--- FAIL: Testéé (0.00s)
'` (valid multibyte) → classified FAIL fine.
  - `'ok  	p\xffkg	0.01s
'` → classified as pass-package: `ESC[32mPASS | p\xffkg ESC[0m
`.
  - `'=== RUN   Test\xff
'` → classified START: `ESC[90mSTART| \xffESC[0m
` (note START label has no space before `|`; `Test` prefix stripped).
  So the FAIL/PASS/SKIP test-name matcher rejects invalid bytes (behaves like a char class matching Unicode letters/digits but not U+FFFD/RuneError), while RUN and `ok`-package matchers tolerate them.
- Styled line shapes observed (default config): PASS test line `ESC[32mPASS | Foo (0.00s)ESC[0m
`; FAIL test line `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | Bar (0.00s)ESC[0m
`; `ok	pkg	...` → `ESC[32mPASS | pkg ESC[0m
` (trailing space after pkg, duration dropped); bare `PASS`/`FAIL` → hidden (no output). `Test` prefix stripped from test names in PASS/FAIL/START lines.

## 3. Trailing-newline rule summary (both modes)

- Plain: stdout = [per ScanLines line: `line
`] + (`
` if input empty or ends with `
`); stderr = `
` always; exit 0.
- Color: stdout = [per non-empty ScanLines line: decorated `line
`]; nothing else; stderr empty; exit 0. Input `''` and `'
'` both produce zero output bytes.

## Ambiguities not fully resolved

- The exact regexes behind the invalid-UTF-8 classification asymmetry (FAIL-name vs RUN/ok) were only probed at the examples above.
- Relative write order of the plain-mode extra stdout `
` vs the stderr `
` couldn't be distinguished; both follow all content.

payload.resultSummary:
All experiments complete, temp dirs cleaned. Here is the full behavioral spec for DOMAIN 4.

# DOMAIN 4 — Style attributes & color syntax (richgo `testfilter`)

All runs used `RICHGO_LOCAL=1 RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` in a `mktemp -d` CWD with a `.richstyle` file; input piped via stdin. Reference input line: `--- PASS: TestFoo (0.00s)\n`, which renders (default) as `ESC[32mPASS | Foo (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`.

## 1. Rendering pipeline per styled line

`<bg-seq?><fg-seq?><attr-seqs...>TEXTESC[0m\n`

- Each component is a SEPARATE escape sequence, emitted in this fixed order:
  1. **background** color (if set)
  2. **foreground** color (if set)
  3. **attributes** in fixed numeric order (regardless of YAML key order)
- Then the decorated text, then a single `ESC[0m` immediately **before** the `\n`.
- If a style is completely empty (no colors, no attrs — e.g. `foreground: ""` with nothing else), NO escapes are emitted at all, not even `ESC[0m`: output is plain `PASS | Foo (0.00s)\n`.
- Config **merges** with built-in defaults field-by-field: setting only `passStyle.bold: true` keeps default green fg → `ESC[32mESC[1m...`. Setting `buildStyle.bold: false` removes the default bold → only `ESC[33m`. `null` values = unset (default kept).

## 2. Boolean attributes (exact codes)

| YAML key | sequence |
|---|---|
| `bold` | `ESC[1m` |
| `faint` | `ESC[2m` |
| `italic` | `ESC[3m` |
| `underline` | `ESC[4m` |
| `blinkSlow` | `ESC[5m` |
| `blinkRapid` | `ESC[6m` |
| `inverse` | `ESC[7m` |
| `conceal` | `ESC[8m` |
| `crossOut` | `ESC[9m` |
| `frame` | `ESC[51m` |
| `encircle` | `ESC[52m` |
| `overline` | `ESC[53m` |

All 13 set at once (YAML in scrambled order) emitted, verbatim:
`ESC[32m ESC[1m ESC[2m ESC[3m ESC[4m ESC[5m ESC[6m ESC[7m ESC[8m ESC[9m ESC[51m ESC[52m ESC[53m PASS | Foo (0.00s) ESC[0m \n`
(fg first because no bg was set). Full combo `background: red, foreground: blue, bold+underline`:
`ESC[41m ESC[34m ESC[1m ESC[4m PASS | Foo (0.00s) ESC[0m \n`

YAML typing: `bold: yes` works (YAML bool); `bold: 1` or `bold: "true"` → whole-file config error (see §6). Unknown keys (e.g. `sparkle: true`) are silently ignored.

## 3. Named colors (case-sensitive; only these exact spellings)

| name | fg | bg |
|---|---|---|
| `black` | 30 | 40 |
| `red` | 31 | 41 |
| `green` | 32 | 42 |
| `yellow` | 33 | 43 |
| `blue` | 34 | 44 |
| `magenta` | 35 | 45 |
| `cyan` | 36 | 46 |
| `white` | 37 | 47 |
| `lightBlack` | 90 | 100 |
| `lightRed` | 91 | 101 |
| `lightGreen` | 92 | 102 |
| `lightYellow` | 93 | 103 |
| `lightBlue` | 94 | 104 |
| `lightMagenta` | 95 | 105 |
| `lightCyan` | 96 | 106 |
| `lightWhite` | 97 | 107 |

- Special name **`default`** = "no color": accepted, emits nothing, and *removes* the inherited default color (`passStyle: {foreground: default, bold: true}` → `ESC[1m...ESC[0m`, no color seq).
- REJECTED (config error, §6): `gray`, `grey`, `lightGray`, `lightGrey`, `darkGray`, `darkGrey`, `Red`, `RED`, `Green`, `LightBlack`, `lightblack`, `White`, `normal`, `orange`, `pink`, `brown`, `purple`, `silver`, `navy`, `teal`, `lime`, `aqua`, `fuchsia`, `maroon`, `olive`, `lightPink`, `darkRed`, `brightRed`, `brightBlack`, `light`, `Light`.

## 4. Hex and rgb() colors

- **`#rrggbb`** (exactly 6 hex digits, `#` required; upper/lower/mixed case OK): fg → `ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm`, bg → `ESC[48;2;R;G;Bm` (decimal components).
  - `#ff0000`/`#FF0000` → `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m`; `#a1B2c3` → `ESC[38;2;161;178;195m`; bg `#00ff10` → `ESC[48;2;0;255;16m`.
  - REJECTED: `#rgb` (`#f00`, `#F00`), `#12345`, `#1234567`, missing `#` (`ff0000`), bad digits (`#gg0000`), `#12`, `#`.
- **`rgb(r,g,b)`** — prefix `rgb` is case-INSENSITIVE (`RGB`, `RgB`, `rGb` all work):
  - Decimal: `rgb(255,0,0)` → `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m`; leading zeros OK (`rgb(001,002,003)` → `1;2;3`); range 0–255 (`rgb(256,0,0)`, `rgb(0377,0,0)`, `rgb(-1,0,0)` rejected).
  - Hex components: `rgb(0xff,0x00,0x00)` → `255;0;0`; `0x`/`0X` OK; **exactly 2 hex digits required** (`rgb(0x01,0x02,0x03)` → `1;2;3`, but `rgb(0x1,0x2,0x3)` and `rgb(0x100,0,0)` rejected).
  - Whitespace: spaces allowed only AFTER commas (`rgb(255, 0, 0)` OK); space after `(`, before `)`, or before a comma (`rgb( 255,...)`, `rgb(255 ,0,0)`, `rgb(255,0,0 )`) rejected. Exactly 3 components required.
- **Integer / 256-palette**: YAML int or quoted numeric string 0–255 → `ESC[38;5;Nm` fg / `ESC[48;5;Nm` bg. Verified 0,7,8,15,16,200,255 OK (both `123` and `"123"`); 256, -1, 1000 → config error.
- Empty string `""` = valid, means no color (like `default`).

## 5. `hide: true` semantics per category

- `hide: true` drops the line's output entirely (nothing, not even newline). Verified for `startStyle`, `passStyle`, `failStyle`, `skipStyle`, `buildStyle` (hides BOTH the `# pkg` header line and the following message lines), `coveredStyle`/`uncoveredStyle` (standalone `coverage: X% of statements` lines), and `passPackageStyle`/`failPackageStyle` (default config already hides both).
- `hide: false` explicitly re-enables: `passPackageStyle: {hide: false}` on input `PASS\n` → `ESC[32mPASSESC[0m\n` (raw text, no label prefix). `failPackageStyle: {hide: false}` on `FAIL\n` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAILESC[0m\n`.
- `fileStyle.hide: true` / `lineStyle.hide: true` don't drop the line; they drop just the filename / `:N:N` segments inside build-error lines (see §7), leaving the rest.
- Note: `ok  \tpkg\t0.1s\tcoverage: 80.0% of statements` lines are NOT affected by covered/uncovered styles at all (they take passPackage green without hiding) — coverage styling only applies to standalone `coverage:` lines.

## 6. Invalid color / config error behavior

- Any invalid color (bad name, bad hex, bad rgb(), out-of-range int) or YAML type error causes the **entire config file to be discarded** — all other valid customizations in the same file are lost and built-in defaults apply. Loading continues with the NEXT file in the search order (verified: bad `.richstyle` + valid `.richstyle.yaml` → the `.yaml` was still applied).
- Error goes to **stderr** via Go `log` (timestamp prefix), exit code stays **0**, processing continues. Exact bytes (one line):
  `2026/08/08 11:23:23 error unmarshaling yaml from /tmp/.../.richstyle :  invalid format\n`
  (note the doubled space: `<path> :␣␣invalid format` — pattern is `... : ` + error text, and the color error text itself is ` invalid format` with a leading space, or equivalent).
- YAML structural/type errors surface the yaml library message after the same prefix, e.g.:
  - `... :  yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 2: cannot unmarshal !!int `1` into bool` (multi-line, literal newlines in the log output)
  - `... :  yaml: line 1: did not find expected ',' or ']'`

## 7. Reset (`ESC[0m`) behavior + the BUILD-line quirk

- Normal styled lines: `ESC[0m` immediately before `\n`.
- **`# pkg` build-header lines: reset comes AFTER the newline** — input `# example/pkg\n` outputs exactly:
  `ESC[33m ESC[1m BUILD| example/pkg \n ESC[0m`
  i.e. the `ESC[0m` dangles at the start of the next line (or at EOF — output ends with `\nESC[0m`, no trailing newline after it; a `\n` is even added if the input lacked one). Every `#`-prefixed line reopens the style (`# a\n# b\n` → two full `BUILD|` blocks each with reset-after-`\n`).
- Build-error message lines (`./main.go:10:2: undefined: foo`) render with a blank label of the same width as `BUILD|` (6 spaces incl. `|`) and nest file/line styles, e.g.:
  `ESC[33m ESC[1m "     | " ESC[36m ./main.go ESC[0m ESC[35m :10:2 ESC[0m ESC[33m ESC[1m : undefined: foo ESC[0m \n`
  — fileStyle span (`./main.go`), reset, lineStyle span (`:10:2`), reset, then buildStyle **re-opened** for the remaining message text (`: undefined: foo`), reset, `\n`. The re-open after the file/line spans is unconditional (still emitted even when fileStyle/lineStyle are `hide: true`; hidden segments themselves emit nothing, not even their text).
- Extra classification note: any otherwise-unrecognized line that FOLLOWS a `# pkg` line is styled as a build-continuation line (blank label + buildStyle, normal reset-before-`\n`).

payload.resultSummary:
# DOMAIN 3 — Config file discovery & parsing: behavioral spec

All experiments run in fresh `mktemp -d` dirs with `env -i` (controlled `HOME`/`GOPATH`/`GOROOT`), `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` unless noted. `/workspace` was never touched. Note: the environment runs as **root**, so a chmod-000 unreadability test was void (root reads anything). Also, during cleanup I mistakenly ran `rm -rf /tmp/tmp.*`, which may have deleted other agents' `/tmp/tmp.*` temp dirs — `/workspace` verified clean (only LICENSE, README.md, .git, executable).

## 1. Discovery paths & precedence

All 12 candidate files from the README are actually probed, in the README's listed order. **Files are deep-merged over the built-in defaults in that order — later files win.** Effective priority, highest first:

`$HOME/.richstyle.yml` > `$HOME/.richstyle.yaml` > `$HOME/.richstyle` > `$GOROOT/.yml` > `$GOROOT/.yaml` > `$GOROOT/.richstyle` > `$GOPATH/.yml` > `$GOPATH/.yaml` > `$GOPATH/.richstyle` > `$CWD/.yml` > `$CWD/.yaml` > `$CWD/.richstyle` > defaults

Verified pairings: CWD<GOPATH (red from GOPATH beat blue from CWD), GOPATH<GOROOT, GOROOT<HOME, CWD<HOME; within one dir: `.richstyle` < `.yaml` < `.yml` (e.g. red in `.richstyle` + blue in `.yaml` → `ESC[34m`; magenta in `.yml` beat both).

- **GOPATH unset or empty string** → falls back to `$HOME/go` (config at `$HOME/go/.richstyle` was loaded).
- **GOPATH with multiple entries** (`gp1:gp2`) is used verbatim as a single path — no splitting; configs in neither entry are found.
- **HOME unset** → HOME configs silently skipped (no error).
- **GOROOT unset** → not directly testable (can't write outside temp); panic stack traces reference `/usr/local/go/src/...`, so the fallback is presumably the build-time GOROOT `/usr/local/go`.
- **RICHGO_LOCAL**: only the exact string `"1"` enables local mode (loads only `$CWD/.richstyle*`, same internal `.yml > .yaml > .richstyle` order; if none exist → defaults). Values `"0"`, `"true"`, `"01"`, `" 1"`, `"2"` all behave as unset.

## 2. Merge semantics

- Merge starts from built-in defaults; each successfully parsed file deep-merges on top.
- **Per-attribute deep merge, across files**: CWD `failStyle.foreground: blue` + GOPATH `failStyle.bold: false` → FAIL line `ESC[34mFAIL | Bad (0.01s)ESC[0m` (both applied). Setting only `failStyle.foreground: blue` keeps default bold → `ESC[34m ESC[1m`.
- Scalar keys (`labelType`, `coverThreshold`, `leaveTestPrefix`) override across files (CWD `labelType: short` + GOPATH `passStyle…` → both applied; HOME `labelType: long` overrode CWD `short`).
- **`removals` lists APPEND across files** (CWD `["OK"]` + GOPATH `["Bad"]` → both removals applied); `removals: []` in a later file does NOT clear earlier ones.
- **Per-file atomicity**: any parse/type error in a file rejects that whole file (valid keys in it are lost), other files still merge. Two invalid files → two error lines, logged in load order, exit 0.

## 3. Errors — all non-fatal EXCEPT bad removals regexp

Stderr uses Go std `log` with `LstdFlags` (local time): `2026/08/08 11:29:28 `. Message formats (exact bytes):

- YAML syntax error: `error unmarshaling yaml from <PATH> :  yaml: line 1: did not find expected ',' or ']'` — note literal ` :  ` (colon + two spaces) before the error. Exit 0, output continues.
- Type mismatch: `... :  yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 1: cannot unmarshal !!str `abc` into int` (multi-line message). Observed target types: `int` (coverThreshold), `bool` (bold), `[]string` (removals), `config.LabelType` (labelType).
- Invalid color (`notacolor`, `rgb(300,0,0)`): `... :  invalid format`.
- `.richstyle` is a directory: `error reading from <PATH> :  read <PATH>: is a directory`.
- **Invalid regexp in `removals` → PANIC (color mode only)**: stderr `panic: regexp: Compile(`[`): error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `[`` + goroutine trace through `regexp.MustCompile`, `github.com/kyoh86/richgo/editor/test.New()` (`/workspace/editor/test/test.go:19`), `main.formatWriteCloser` (`main.go:86`), `main.main` (`main.go:60`). **Exit code 2, no stdout.** In pass-through mode, no panic.
- Unknown keys (top-level or nested in a style): silently ignored. Keys are **case-sensitive lowercase** (`PassStyle:`, `PASSSTYLE:` ignored).
- Empty file / comment-only file: OK, defaults used.

## 4. Value semantics

- **labelType**: exact `"long"` → `PASS | OK (0.00s)`; exact `"short"` → `o  OK (0.00s)` (char + 2 spaces); **any other scalar value** (`none`, `bogus`, `Long`, `SHORT`, `0`, `1`, `2`, `5`) → no label, no error. A sequence (`[a]`) → unmarshal error into `config.LabelType`.
- **coverThreshold**: `int` field. Quoted `"60"` → type error. Floats (`60.5`, `60.9`) accepted **silently**; effective comparison is integer-truncated: covered iff `int(coverage) >= int(threshold)` (60.0% vs 60.9 → covered/green; 60.0 vs 60 → covered). `150` and `-10` accepted, no clamping (60% vs 150 → uncovered style `ESC[33m ESC[1m`).
- **Bools**: unquoted `yes` → true (YAML 1.1); quoted `"yes"` → `cannot unmarshal !!str `yes` into bool`.
- **Colors**: names (`red`→`ESC[31m`); bare int `123` → `ESC[38;5;123m`; `"#ff0000"` → `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m`; `rgb(1,2,3)` → `ESC[38;2;1;2;3m`; `rgb(0x10,0x20,0x30)` → `ESC[38;2;16;32;48m`. Out-of-range/unknown → `invalid format` (whole file rejected).
- **SGR emission order**: background, then foreground, then one escape per attribute, text, `ESC[0m` at end (e.g. `ESC[44m ESC[38;2;16;32;48m…ESC[0m`; default failStyle = `ESC[31m ESC[1m`).
- `hide: true` → line suppressed entirely (empty output for that line). `leaveTestPrefix: true` → `PASS | TestOK (0.00s)` (prefix kept).

## 5. Pass-through (non-color) mode interplay

- Config files are **still read and parse errors still logged** to stderr, but nothing from config affects output.
- Output = verbatim copy of stdin **plus exactly one extra `\n` appended at EOF** (even for empty stdin → output is just `\n`; `line1\nline2` (no trailing NL) → `line1\nline2\n`). Exit 0.
- `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR`: **any non-empty value enables color** (`0`, `true` both colorized); empty string = unset.

payload.resultSummary:
All experiments complete and temp dir cleaned. Here is the behavioral spec for Domain 5.

# DOMAIN 5 — `removals` & `leaveTestPrefix` — Behavioral Spec

Test harness: temp dir with `RICHGO_LOCAL=1` to isolate config; `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` for styled mode. Escapes shown as `ESC[...m`. All exit codes captured via pipe status, not the downstream pager.

## 1. `leaveTestPrefix`

**Only affects styled (colorized) output.** In plain mode (no TTY, no FORCE_COLOR) output is always byte-verbatim pass-through regardless of this setting.

- Default (`false` or absent): the literal prefix `Test` is stripped from the **first component only** of the test name on classified test lines (RUN/PASS/FAIL/SKIP). With `true`, the name is kept whole.
- The classification itself requires the name to begin with literal `Test` (case-sensitive) — with or without `leaveTestPrefix`:
  - `=== RUN   Testfoo` → `ESC[90mSTART| fooESC[0m`; `Testify` → `ify`; `Test` → `START| ` (empty name); `TestTest` → `Test` (only the first `Test` stripped).
  - `=== RUN   TEST`, `BenchmarkX`, `ExampleFoo`, `FuzzFoo` are **not classified at all** — they fall through to the "unknown line" rendering: `ESC[90m     | === RUN   TESTESC[0m` (5-space empty label + `| ` + raw line verbatim).
- Subtests: `TestFoo/SubBar` → `Foo/SubBar` (default) / `TestFoo/SubBar` (true). `TestFoo/TestSub` → `Foo/TestSub` — a `Test` prefix on later path components is never stripped. Output indent is depth-based, not from source whitespace: depth-1 → `START|   Foo/SubBar` (3 spaces), depth-2 → `START|     Foo/a_b/c` (5 spaces; i.e. 1+2·depth). This applied identically to `    --- PASS: TestFoo/SubBar (0.00s)` → `PASS |   Foo/SubBar (0.00s)`.
- Applies to RUN, PASS, FAIL, SKIP lines equally (`--- FAIL: TestFoo/SubFail (0.02s)` → `FAIL |   Foo/SubFail (0.02s)` / `FAIL |   TestFoo/SubFail (0.02s)`).
- Does **not** affect package lines (`PASS`, `ok  \tpkg\t0.012s`, `FAIL\tpkg\t0.005s`), file lines, or cover lines — verified byte-identical between true/false.
- `leaveTestPrefix: yes` is accepted as true (YAML 1.1 bool), exit 0.

## 2. `removals`

**Key finding: removals are regexp *substring deletions* applied to the fully rendered output line — after classification, labeling, Test-stripping, inner file/line styling, AND after the outer ANSI color escapes have been prepended/appended. They are not applied to raw input, and they are applied *only in colorized mode* (plain mode ignores them completely — output stays verbatim).**

Mechanics (each rule below is experimentally verified):

- Each entry is compiled with Go `regexp.MustCompile` (RE2 syntax), then applied via `ReplaceAllString(renderedLine, "")`, **sequentially in list order**:
  - `removals: [Foo, oo]` on rendered `PASS | Foo (0.00s)` → `PASS |  (0.00s)`; `[oo, Foo]` → `PASS | F (0.00s)`.
- Matching is unanchored substring. Because the target string starts with `ESC[` and ends with `ESC[0m`:
  - `^FAIL`, `^PASS`, `^START`, `^ ` **never match** (nothing is at position 0 except ESC).
  - `$` effectively never matches mid-ANSI (`0\.00s$` no-op; `^FAIL.*$` no-op).
  - Removals can corrupt the escapes: `32m` turned `ESC[32mPASS | Foo...` into `ESC[PASS | Foo...` (literal output bytes: `^[[PASS | Foo (0.00s)^[[0m`). This proves application after ANSI insertion.
- Examples (color mode, default config, removal `PASS`):
  - `--- PASS: TestFoo (0.00s)` → `ESC[32m | Foo (0.00s)ESC[0m` (label hit; note this also proves application *after* Test-stripping — content was already `Foo`).
  - `ok  \texample.com/pkg\t0.012s` → `ESC[32m | example.com/pkg ESC[0m` (the `PASS` label of the package line was hit even though the raw line contains no "PASS" — proves application after label rendering).
  - `another line with PASS inside` → `another line with  inside`.
- **Line dropping**: if the post-removal string is exactly empty, the line is omitted entirely (no newline). `removals: [".*"]` → total output is **zero bytes**. If anything remains — even only escapes — it is printed: removing `FAIL \| Bar \(0\.00s\)` leaves `ESC[31mESC[1mESC[0m\n`. (Corollary: blank input lines are also dropped in color mode; in plain mode they pass through.)
- Multiple regexps: all apply (e.g. `[START, FAIL]` blanks both labels: `ESC[90m| FooESC[0m`, `ESC[31mESC[1m | Bar (0.00s)ESC[0m`).
- Applies to every rendered line category: file lines (`foo_test` removed inside the cyan segment: `ESC[36m.goESC[0m`) and cover lines (`45` → `COVER| .0% [####______]`).
- Interaction with `leaveTestPrefix`: removals see the post-transform text. With `leaveTestPrefix: true` + removal `TestF`: `TestFoo/TestSub` → `oo/TestSub`; with default false, removal `TestF` finds nothing (`Foo/TestSub` unchanged).
- Interaction with `hide`: bare `PASS` package line vanishes under default config (`passPackageStyle.hide: true`) independently of removals.

## 3. Errors & exit codes

- **Invalid regexp** (valid YAML, e.g. `removals: ["["]`): Go panic on **stderr**, exit code **2**:
  ```
  panic: regexp: Compile(`[`): error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `[`
  goroutine 1 [running]:
  regexp.MustCompile({0x61baf8, 0x1})  /usr/local/go/src/regexp/regexp.go:319
  github.com/kyoh86/richgo/editor/test.New()  /workspace/editor/test/test.go:19
  main.formatWriteCloser(...)  /workspace/main.go:86
  main.main()  /workspace/main.go:60
  ```
  (Stack trace reveals internal structure: `editor/test.New()` compiles removals at test.go:19.)
- **YAML syntax/escape error** (e.g. double-quoted `"FAIL \| Bar"` or `"\x1b..."`): logged to **stderr** with `log` timestamp prefix, exit code **0**, processing continues with **default config**:
  `2026/08/08 11:24:55 error unmarshaling yaml from /tmp/.../.richstyle :  yaml: line 2: found unknown escape character` (note the literal ` :  ` — space colon two spaces).
- **YAML escaping rules for regexps**: unquoted (`- 0\.00s`) and single-quoted (`- '0\.00s$'`) preserve backslashes — both work. Double-quoted scalars reject `\d`, `\|`, `\x1b`, etc. ("found unknown escape character"). Numeric entries (`- 123`) are silently coerced to the string `"123"` and work (removal `123` turned `TestFoo123` → `Foo`).

## 4. Side observations (adjacent domains, noted for the implementer)

- Plain mode appends one extra `\n` at EOF (empty input → single `\n`); color mode does not (empty input → zero bytes).
- Rendered label format: word padded to width 5 + `| ` — `START| `, `PASS | `, `FAIL | `, `SKIP | `, `COVER| `, unknown `     | `.
- "Unknown" lines inherit the previously used category's color (lightBlack after START, green after PASS, etc.) — observed but not fully characterized; left to the styling-domain agent.

payload.resultSummary:
# DOMAIN 6 Behavioral Spec: `test` subcommand, delegation, exit codes, TTY detection

Environment used: go1.21.0 linux/amd64, temp module `example.com/probe` with `passpkg` (TestAdd pass, TestSkip skip), `failpkg` (TestFail fails), `builderr` (syntax error), `GOPROXY=off GOFLAGS=-mod=mod`.

## 1. Command dispatch

- `richgo test ...` → runs `go test ...` with **args passed through verbatim** (no `-v` or any flag added/removed/reordered). Evidence: `richgo test -count=1 ./passpkg/` non-color stdout is byte-identical to `go test -count=1 ./passpkg/` (modulo trailing-newline quirk below); `-run`, `-v`, `-json` all honored; `richgo test --help` is byte-identical to `go test --help` (usage on **stderr**, exit **2**).
- `richgo testfilter [any extra args ignored]` → reads stdin, writes filtered stdout. Extra args (`testfilter foo bar`) silently ignored, exit 0. Never touches `go` (works with empty PATH).
- Any other first arg (`version`, `env GOPATH`, `build`, `frobnicate`, no args) → delegated to `go` with direct stream attachment (no filtering/styling ever), byte-identical output, exit code propagated:
  - `richgo version` → `go version go1.21.0 linux/amd64\n`, exit 0.
  - `richgo frobnicate` → stderr `go frobnicate: unknown command\nRun 'go help' for usage.\n`, exit **2** (same as `go frobnicate`).
  - `richgo` (no args) → go usage text on stderr (1804 bytes), exit **2**.
- `go` is located via **PATH lookup** (a symlink `go` in a custom PATH dir works). If `go` is not in PATH, richgo **panics** (exit **2**):
  - delegated cmd: stdout empty, stderr = `panic: exec: "go": executable file not found in $PATH\n\ngoroutine 1 [running]:\nmain.main()\n\t/workspace/main.go:74 +0x465\n`
  - `test`: stdout = `\n`, stderr = `\n` + same panic text (both filter streams emit their EOF newline first).

## 2. Colorize decision — keyed on **stderr**, not stdout (quirk!)

Colorization is ON iff `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR` env var is **set to any non-empty string** (`1`, `0`, `false`, `garbage`, `TRUE`, `2` all enable; empty string and unset do not) **OR fd 2 (stderr) is a TTY** (real isatty check: `/dev/null` does not trigger). `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` are ignored.

Verified asymmetry (no force var):
- `richgo test`/`testfilter` with stdout=file, **stderr=PTY** → output written to the file is **fully styled with ANSI escapes**.
- stdout=PTY, **stderr=file** → output on the PTY is **plain** (non-color mode).

The decision is global: when on, BOTH the stdout-filter and stderr-filter of `richgo test` style their content; when off, both pass through.

## 3. `richgo test` plumbing

Runs `go test` with stdout→filter→richgo's stdout and stderr→filter→richgo's stderr (build errors, which `go test` writes to stderr, are styled in color mode: `ESC[33mESC[1mBUILD| example.com/probe/builderr\nESC[0m...`).

Exit code = go test's exit code exactly: pass→0, test failure→1, build error→1, `test --help`→2, bad usage→1/2 as go does.

**Trailing-newline quirk (deterministic, verified with 2s-slow tests):**
- go test **succeeds** (exit 0): each filter, in **non-color mode only**, appends exactly one extra `\n` at EOF. So stdout = go's stdout + `\n`; stderr (usually empty from go) = `\n`. Example: `richgo test -count=1 ./passpkg/` (stdout & stderr split, non-color) → stdout `ok  \texample.com/probe/passpkg\t0.002s\n\n`, stderr `\n`, exit 0. In color mode: no extra bytes (`ESC[32mPASS  | example.com/probe/passpkg ESC[0m\n`, stderr empty).
- go test **fails** (exit≠0): the extra EOF newline is **suppressed on both streams** — stdout/stderr are exactly the filter output with no trailing addition (non-color: byte-identical to `go test`; color: styled, hidden lines removed).

## 4. Filter behavior (applies to `testfilter` and `richgo test`'s pipe)

Non-color mode = **byte-for-byte pass-through of every line** (no hiding, no labels, `=== RUN`/`PASS`/`FAIL` all verbatim), with this EOF rule: every input line is terminated (a final unterminated line gets `\n` appended); then, iff input was empty or ended with `\n`, one extra `\n` is written. Verified: `''`→`\n`; `hello`→`hello\n`; `hello\n`→`hello\n\n`; `\n`→`\n\n`; `hello\nworld\n`→`hello\nworld\n\n`.

Color mode (representative exact bytes, default styles):
- `ok  \tfoo\t0.1s\n` → `ESC[32mPASS  | foo ESC[0m\n` (timing replaced by single trailing space; standalone `PASS` line hidden entirely — `hide:true`)
- `FAIL\texample.com/probe/failpkg\t0.002s\n` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL  | \texample.com/probe/failpkg\t0.002sESC[0m\n`; standalone `FAIL` lines hidden
- `=== RUN   TestAdd\n` → `ESC[90mSTART| AddESC[0m\n` (`Test` prefix stripped)
- `--- PASS: TestAdd (0.00s)\n` → `ESC[32mPASS  | Add (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`
- test log line `    pass_test.go:12: skipping\n` → `ESC[90m     |     ESC[36mpass_test.goESC[0mESC[35m:12ESC[0mESC[90m: skippingESC[0m\n` (blank 5-space label + `| `; file cyan, `:12` magenta)
- uncategorized lines (e.g. `-json` output) → prefixed with blank label `     | ` (5 spaces, pipe, space), no escapes
- `testfilter` exit code is **always 0**, even for `FAIL` input.

## 5. Notes for the implementer

- The panic on missing `go` (message text + exit code 2) should be reproduced; the goroutine trace path/offset (`/workspace/main.go:74 +0x465`) is build-specific.
- The stderr-based TTY check looks like an upstream bug but is 100% deterministic — reproduce it exactly (isatty on fd 2).
- The "extra `\n` on success only" behavior of `richgo test` suggests: filter EOF-finalization runs only when exit code is 0; on failure richgo exits without it. In color mode the EOF newline never happens.
- Config files (`.richstyle*`) were not created anywhere; `/workspace` untouched; all temp dirs cleaned up.

All probes complete and temp dirs cleaned up. Here is the full behavioral spec for Domain 1.

# DOMAIN 1 REPORT — default-config `testfilter` line classification & rendering

Setup: empty CWD (no `.richstyle*`), `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`, input piped to `/workspace/executable testfilter`. Escapes written as `ESC[..m`. Reset is always `ESC[0m`.

## Global structure

- Output line skeleton: `STYLE? LABEL| indent CONTENT ESC[0m? \n`, where `LABEL` is padded to **5 chars**, immediately followed by `|` (no space): `PASS |`, `FAIL |`, `SKIP |`, `START|`, `BUILD|`.
- Unrecognized ("plain") lines get prefix `     | ` — exactly **5 spaces + `| `** — i.e. the `|` sits in the same column as for labels.
- Input is processed line-by-line; `\n` and a trailing `\r` are stripped (CRLF input renders as plain LF output). An unterminated final line still gets a `\n` appended.
- Completely empty input lines (`\n` only) produce **zero output bytes** (dropped). Whitespace-only lines are plain lines (`   \n` → `     |    \n`).
- Exit code is **0 in all cases** (FAIL content, empty input, etc.).

## Context-color state machine (important!)

Every styled status line sets a persistent "current style". All subsequent **plain** lines are wrapped in that style (including their `     | ` prefix) until the next status line changes it:

- `=== RUN`/`--- SKIP`/`? [no test files]` → `ESC[90m`
- `--- PASS`/`ok` → `ESC[32m`
- `--- FAIL`/`FAIL<pkg>` → `ESC[31mESC[1m`
- `# <pkg>` → `ESC[33mESC[1m`
- Hidden lines (bare `PASS`/`FAIL`) and blank lines do **not** change it. Initial state = no style.

Example: `--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)\nlog line\n` →
`ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n` then `ESC[31mESC[1m     | log lineESC[0m\n`.
Context persists across blank lines; `ok ...` after FAIL switches context to green, etc.

## Category 1 — `=== RUN` → START

- Regex ≈ `^=== RUN   (Test.*)$` — **exactly 3 spaces**, column 0, name must start with `Test`.
- Output: `ESC[90mSTART|` + N spaces + `<name minus leading "Test">` + `ESC[0m\n`, where **N = 1 + 2×(number of `/` in the name)**.
  - `=== RUN   TestX` → `ESC[90mSTART| XESC[0m\n`
  - `=== RUN   TestX/A/B` → `START|     X/A/B` (5 spaces)
  - `=== RUN   Test` → `ESC[90mSTART| ESC[0m\n` (name strips to empty; the 1 space remains)
  - `=== RUN   Test X` → `START|  X` (remainder ` X` kept verbatim)
- NOT matched (→ plain): 1/2/4 spaces or tab after `RUN`; any leading indentation; names starting `Example`/`Benchmark`/`Fuzz`/`Foo`.
- `=== PAUSE   TestX`, `=== CONT   TestX`, `=== NAME   TestX` are **not** recognized → plain lines.

## Category 2 — test result lines `--- PASS/FAIL/SKIP`

- Regex ≈ `^( *)--- (PASS|FAIL|SKIP): (Test.*)$` (space after colon required; name must start `Test`; time NOT required — `--- PASS: TestX` matches and `--- PASS: TestX (0.00s) trailing` keeps everything after the name verbatim).
- **Input indentation (spaces) is discarded**; output indent is recomputed from slashes exactly like RUN: N = 1 + 2×depth spaces after `|`.
  - `--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)` → `ESC[32mPASS | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`
  - `    --- PASS: TestX/Sub (0.00s)` → `ESC[32mPASS |   X/Sub (0.00s)ESC[0m\n` (3 spaces)
  - `--- FAIL: TestX (0.01s)` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | X (0.01s)ESC[0m\n`
  - `--- SKIP: TestX (0.00s)` → `ESC[90mSKIP | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`
- **Tab-indented fallback**: if the leading whitespace contains a tab (`\t--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)`, ` \t--- PASS: TestX ...`), the label/style is applied but the **entire original line is kept as content** (no Test-strip, no reindent): `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | \t--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`. Still requires `: ` + `Test` (`\t--- PASS: Foo` and `\t--- PASS:TestX` → plain). Sets context normally.

356	
357	- Each entry is compiled with Go `regexp.MustCompile` (RE2 syntax), then applied via `ReplaceAllString(renderedLine, "")`, **sequentially in list order**:
358	  - `removals: [Foo, oo]` on rendered `PASS | Foo (0.00s)` → `PASS |  (0.00s)`; `[oo, Foo]` → `PASS | F (0.00s)`.

361	  - `$` effectively never matches mid-ANSI (`0\.00s$` no-op; `^FAIL.*$` no-op).
362	  - Removals can corrupt the escapes: `32m` turned `ESC[32mPASS | Foo...` into `ESC[PASS | Foo...` (literal output bytes: `^[[PASS | Foo (0.00s)^[[0m`). This proves application after ANSI insertion.

453	## 1. Plain (non-color) mode — line processing + verbatim passthrough
454	
455	**Core rule:** input is processed line-by-line with exactly `bufio.ScanLines` semantics (split on `\n`; strip at most ONE trailing `\r` per line, including a lone `\r` at EOF). Each resulting line is written to stdout as `line + "\n"`, **completely verbatim otherwise — zero classification, zero styling, zero hiding** (bare `PASS`/`FAIL`/`ok pkg` lines pass through untouched). Then:
456	
457	- **stdout gets one extra `\n` iff the input was empty OR ended with `\n`.**
458	- **stderr always gets exactly one `\n`** at the end (regardless of input).
459	- Exit code always `0` (even for binary garbage, NUL bytes, 100MB lines).
460	
461	Exact byte matrix (stdout shown; stderr is always `\n`):
462	
463	| input | stdout bytes | why |
464	|---|---|---|
465	| `''` | `0a` | no lines + extra `\n` (empty input) |
466	| `'\n'` | `0a 0a` | one empty line + extra `\n` |
467	| `'a'` | `61 0a` | one line, no trailing-NL so no extra |
468	| `'a\n'` | `61 0a 0a` | one line + extra |
469	| `'a\nb'` | `61 0a 62 0a` | no extra |
470	| `'a\nb\n'` | `61 0a 62 0a 0a` | extra |
471	| `'a\n\n'` | `61 0a 0a 0a` | empty line preserved + extra |
472	| `'\n\n'` | `0a 0a 0a` | |
473	| `'\r'` | `0a` | lone `\r` at EOF stripped → one empty line, no trailing-NL → no extra |
474	| `'\r\n'` | `0a 0a` | CR stripped, ends with `\n` → extra |
475	| `'a\r\nb\r\n'` | `61 0a 62 0a 0a` | CRs stripped |
476	| `'a\r\r\n'` | `61 0d 0a 0a` | **only one** trailing CR stripped per line |
477	| `'a\rb\n'` | `61 0d 62 0a 0a` | interior `\r` preserved verbatim |
478	| `'   \n\t\n'` | `20 20 20 0a 09 0a 0a` | whitespace-only lines preserved |
479	| `'a\xff\xfe\n\x80\n'` | `61 ff fe 0a 80 0a 0a` | invalid UTF-8 verbatim, exit 0 |
480	| `'a\x00b\n'` | `61 00 62 0a 0a` | NUL verbatim |
481	
482	With `2>&1`, `'a\n'` yields `61 0a 0a 0a` — both trailing newlines come after all content (order between the stdout extra and the stderr one not distinguishable this way).

484	**No size limit:** single lines of 65535/65536/65537/70000/1MiB/10MiB/100MiB bytes all pass through fine (output = input+1 byte), exit 0, stderr `\n`. 485	
486	## 2. Color mode (`RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`) — edge cases
487	
488	Same ScanLines splitting and one-CR stripping, but semantics differ from plain mode:
489	
490	- **No extra trailing newline, nothing on stderr, ever.** Output is exactly one decorated line per kept input line.
491	- **Empty lines (zero-length after CR-strip) are dropped entirely**: `''`→empty, `'\n'`→empty, `'\n\n\n'`→empty, `'a\n\nb\n'`→ only the `a` and `b` lines.
492	- **Whitespace-only lines are NOT empty** and get the uncategorized treatment: `'   '`→`20 20 20 20 20 7c 20 20 20 20 0a` (`"     |    \n"`), `'\t'`→`"     | \t\n"`.
493	- **Uncategorized lines** are emitted as `20 20 20 20 20 7c 20` + line + `0a` — i.e. 5 spaces, `|`, space (long-label column, blank label), NO color escapes, content verbatim (including invalid UTF-8, NUL, interior `\r`).
494	- `'a'` vs `'a\n'` → identical output (`     | a\n`); trailing newline of input is irrelevant in color mode.
495	- CRLF: `\r` stripped before classification — `'a\r\nb\r\n'`→`     | a\n     | b\n`; `PASS\r\nFAIL\r\n`→ **empty output** (bare PASS/FAIL still hidden per default config). 496	- Invalid UTF-8 bytes never cause errors (exit 0) and are passed through verbatim, but they **can affect classification**:
497	  - `'--- FAIL: T\xffest (0.00s)\n'` → NOT classified (falls to `     | --- FAIL: T\xffest (0.00s)`).
498	  - `'--- FAIL: TestBar (0.00s)\xff\n'` → classified FAIL; the `\xff` is emitted inside the style: `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | Bar (0.00s)\xffESC[0m\n`.
499	  - `'--- FAIL: Testéé (0.00s)\n'` (valid multibyte) → classified FAIL fine.
500	  - `'ok  \tp\xffkg\t0.01s\n'` → classified as pass-package: `ESC[32mPASS | p\xffkg ESC[0m\n`.
501	  - `'=== RUN   Test\xff\n'` → classified START: `ESC[90mSTART| \xffESC[0m\n` (note START label has no space before `|`; `Test` prefix stripped).
502	  So the FAIL/PASS/SKIP test-name matcher rejects invalid bytes (behaves like a char class matching Unicode letters/digits but not U+FFFD/RuneError), while RUN and `ok`-package matchers tolerate them.
503	- Styled line shapes observed (default config): PASS test line `ESC[32mPASS | Foo (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`; FAIL test line `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | Bar (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`; `ok\tpkg\t...` → `ESC[32mPASS | pkg ESC[0m\n` (trailing space after pkg, duration dropped); bare `PASS`/`FAIL` → hidden (no output). `Test` prefix stripped from test names in PASS/FAIL/START lines.
504	
505	## 3. Trailing-newline rule summary (both modes)
506	
507	- Plain: stdout = [per ScanLines line: `line\n`] + (`\n` if input empty or ends with `\n`); stderr = `\n` always; exit 0.
508	- Color: stdout = [per non-empty ScanLines line: decorated `line\n`]; nothing else; stderr empty; exit 0. Input `''` and `'\n'` both produce zero output bytes.
509	
510	## Ambiguities not fully resolved
511	
512	- The exact regexes behind the invalid-UTF-8 classification asymmetry (FAIL-name vs RUN/ok) were only probed at the examples above.
513	- Relative write order of the plain-mode extra stdout `\n` vs the stderr `\n` couldn't be distinguished; both follow all content.</subagent>
